headline: This law requires the FBI to use specialized child-abuse investigation teams and extends federal grants for children's advocacy centers through 2028.
what_it_does: The FBI must use a multidisciplinary team and a trained child forensic interviewer in investigations of child sexual exploitation, abuse, child sexual abuse material, and child trafficking. These requirements do not apply if such a team or interviewer is unavailable or would conflict with federal law. The law also reauthorizes grants for regional and local children's advocacy centers, which coordinate investigation, treatment, and prosecution of child abuse cases, through fiscal year 2028. It adds new grant goals such as supporting state chapters, building a network of care for abuse victims, and setting practice standards.

who_it_affects.group: Children who are victims of abuse, exploitation, or trafficking
who_it_affects.how: FBI child-abuse investigations must use a multidisciplinary team and a trained child forensic interviewer when those requirements can be met.
These centers can receive federal grants through fiscal year 2028, and regional centers are asked to support state chapters.
They must coordinate with multidisciplinary teams, often based at advocacy centers, in covered cases unless a team or interviewer is unavailable.

who_it_affects.group: Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention
who_it_affects.how: This office must administer the advocacy center grants under the new program goals and selection criteria.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 5, 2023; grant reauthorization runs through fiscal year 2028.
